If it's only an issue with music (ie. no stuttering in audio from a browser), I would first look at pulseaudio. Maybe it's set to the wrong bitrate.

Try setting default-sample-rate = 48000 in /etc/pulse/daemon.conf and restart pulseaudio.

You might also want to try setting it in openal's config, too, in /etc/openal/alsoft.conf with frequency = 48000.

If it's happening on everything in the desktop, then check that the there's no interference (ie. wireless and bluetooth are on difference frequencies). Also, try moving the dongle (if the bluetooth receiver isn't built in) to a different usb port.

If it's still a problem, you can try adjusting the latency of the headset. But you would need to play with the values because too large and the audio will be out of sync with any video.

pacmd list-sinks | egrep -o 'bluez_card[^>]*' to get the bluetooth identifier. Then pactl set-port-latency-offset <bluez_card> headset-output 125000 to set the latency. Replace <bluez_card> with the id from the previous command, and play with 125000 going up or down to make it work best it can. When you find the right one, put it in /etc/pulse/daemon.conf and restart pulseaudio.
